EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
The 2027 Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream Holds Its Own as the Most Beautiful Travel Trailer Around
17 photos
Photo: Airstream
There's always room for improvement, as the saying goes. That's true, but not where it concerns "the perfect" Airstream, because obviously, perfection can't be improved. Case in point: the limited edition Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream, now at the 2027 model year.
Airstream announced the Frank Lloyd Wright Limited Edition in the summer of 2025, for what was then the 2026 model year. They said from the start that this series would be limited to just 200 units, parsed out over several years, which bring us to today.
This special edition Airstream is now at the 2027 model year and it's yet to reach the 100th unit. This being such a rare and absolutely beautiful Airstream , taking it in visually is better than nothing at all, so take a few minutes to revisit it with me. Below is the 81st unit built, presented with the purpose of securing a buyer.
The 2027 Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream is more of the same, which is a delicate way of saying that nothing has changed about it from the debut year. Actually, strike that: something did change – not with the trailer itself but pricing, which now starts higher than it did last year.
Photo: Airstream Still, this is, without a doubt, the most beautiful Airstream ever created, and quite possibly one of the most beautiful travel trailers around.
Frank Lloyd Wright is one of the best known and internationally appreciated American architects and designer. His particular style, called organic architecture, embraced core principles like harmony with nature, total, cohesive design where every bit was considered an integral part of the architectural piece, the concept of compression and release, and the so-called "destruction of the box," where isolated rooms were replaced by spaces that flowed one into the other.
All these are apparent in the Frank Lloyd Wright-badged Airstream , which was designed in collaboration with the Lloyd Wright Foundation. Also called the Frank Lloyd Wright Usonian Limited Edition 28RB, it's built on the same body as the International 28RB or the Globetrotter 27FB, but with a fully custom floorplan that makes it the only Airstream with a king bedroom.
Photo: Airstream Inc. This Airstream sits on a boxed steel frame and features the iconic "silver bullet" aluminum body over an aluminum ribbed frame, with composite flooring, full insulation throughout, and the Airstream windows, including the staple Vista View clerestory-style windows, with tinted glass, integrated bug screens, and hand-rived aluminum frames.
Riding on twin axles with Dexter spring suspension and self-adjusting brakes, the Airstream gets power stabilizer jacks, manual awnings on three sides, and rock stone guards on both the body and the front windows. Overall length is 28 feet 2 inches (8.5 meters), and you get 6.7 feet (2 meters) of headroom inside, and 8 feet (2.4 meters) in width, so there's enough space to actually build an architectural, home-like, gorgeous space.
The chassis being similar to that on an International 28RB, you get a tailgate entry that allows you to open up the rear of the trailer to the elements – and whatever view you happen to be parked by. The main bedroom is at the back, but you wouldn't be able to tell it in day mode, as you get a pair of face-to-face comfy sofas that turn this into the second lounge available onboard.
Photo: Airstream Inc. The first one is at the entrance: a beautiful couch wrapping around the front end and turning into a double bed only when needed. In Frank Lloyd Wright style, this Airstream combines materials and fabrics and colors in unexpected ways, to incredible results.
The geometric pattern on the inside of the entry door and laser-cut into the screen door is also found in the dining table, on the kitchen backsplash, and on light fixtures. You have aluminum walls, as you'd expect in an Airstream, but also custom cabinetry of real wood, composite surfaces, and luscious, light fabrics, all of them made to look their best with indirect lighting.
Storage is limited to the lower part of the trailer , with the exception of the narrow hallway that connects the two living areas, where you have floor to ceiling storage across the bathroom. This Special Edition also strives to hide everything you don't want to see from sight, so the TV and sound system, the fridge, and even the dining table are masked from sight by natural wood.
Photo: Airstream Inc. The galley is on the campside, with a three-burner gas cooktop and a massive stainless steel sink set into a composite countertop with beautiful wood finish. Below, you get a convection microwave with an air fryer function and plenty of storage for the basics.
Across the way is an extended counter that hides an extendable dining table and a fold-up workstation. Also built into it is storage for two expandable wooden chairs, so in between the couch, a small footstool, and these two chairs, you can host a nice dinner or gaming party.
The TV and Bluetooth stereo sound is behind a hinged wooden door on the wall. Airstream uses the same kind of door, only of a much bigger size, for the wardrobe, thus coming up with a very discreet solution to a practical, everyday feature.
Photo: Airstream Inc. The bathroom is behind a black panel wall with wooden slats and a smoked porthole with the same geometrical motif. It's a full, three-piece bathroom with a macerator-style porcelain toilet, a stainless steel sink with integrated storage, and a walk-in shower with a seat.
Nice details, like a sliding medicine cabinet door that reveals access to the porthole window, and another matching light fixture, add extra style to a space you wouldn't normally think of in terms of "stylish."
The rear lounge offers sleeping in separate twin beds or in a full king, as the couches join in the middle at the press of a button. Airstream builds storage under each for the essentials, adding an extra-wide open shelf at the back for more items you will want handy.
Photo: Airstream Inc. This Airstream comes started with a 15,000-BTU Coleman-Mach AC in the back and a 13,500-BTU unit in the front, both ducted and with heat pumps, a 30,000-BTU furnace that also heats the holding tanks, a MaxxAir power fan with a rain sensor, an Aqua-hot tankless water heater, a full-size spare on an undermounted carrier, and a solar system with 300W of solar on the roof, a 2000W inverter, and a pair of 500kWh batteries.
In terms of holding tanks, you get 37 gallons (140 liters) for freshwater, 40 gallons (151 liters) for gray, and 35 gallons (132 liters) for black water.
The Frank Lloyd Wright Airstream comes in at 6,900 lbs (3,130 kg) dry and has a gross vehicle weight of 7,600 lbs (3,447 kg), so you have about 700 lbs (317 kg) of cargo carrying capacity.
Photo: Airstream Inc. Starting price has gone up since the last time we looked at this special edition and now sits at $189,900. It's true that each unit is a complete solution, ready to hit the road from the moment of delivery, but you can still add other Frank Lloyd Wright-branded items like cutting boards, exterior graphics, and a teak shower mat, and all these will add to the final sale price.
